Per-feature probability contribution to the composite p_joint.

Exposes the individual feature probabilities that are multiplied
together to form p_joint. Useful for debugging and method development:
understanding which features contributed how much evidence.

See: docs/same_individual_assessment_spec.md § Probability estimation
FeatureContribution.title: FeatureContribution

Inconsistency.description:
A detected inconsistency between two reports.

See: docs/same_individual_assessment_spec.md § Inconsistency Detection
Inconsistency.title: Inconsistency

InconsistencyCounts.description:
Summary counts of inconsistencies by severity level.

Decisive inconsistencies (e.g. distinct patient IDs from the
same study identified in the narratives) override all other
evidence and force a Different individuals classification.
InconsistencyCounts.title: InconsistencyCounts

InconsistencySeverity.description:
Severity levels for detected inconsistencies between reports.

See: docs/same_individual_assessment_spec.md § Severity Levels

Levels:
    minor     – small difference, weakly suggests different individuals
    moderate  – meaningful difference, weakens the duplicate hypothesis
    strong    – strongly suggests different individuals
    decisive  – forces Different classification (e.g. distinct
                patient IDs from the same study in the narratives)
InconsistencySeverity.title: InconsistencySeverity

NarrativeConsistency.description:
Narrative consistency categories from LLM assessment.

See: docs/same_individual_assessment_spec.md § Narrative Consistency Assessment

Values
------
STRONGLY_CONSISTENT : narratives clearly describe the same patient
CONSISTENT : probable but not certain match
NEUTRAL : narratives too sparse to judge
INCONSISTENT : narratives clearly describe different patients
NOT_AVAILABLE : LLM assessment was not performed or failed
NarrativeConsistency.title: NarrativeConsistency
